title: Rav Beruna
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was a distinguished student of Rav, as stated explicitly in [Pesachim 103a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.103a.10-103b.1): Rav Beruna and Rav Chananel, Rav’s students, were sitting at a meal; Rav Yeiva Saba was attending them; they said to him, “Give us [the cup] and let us bless,” etc. In [Yevamot 110a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.110a.5): a certain case that occurred in Naresh, where a girl was betrothed while a minor … and Rav Beruna and Rav Chananel, Rav’s students, were there, etc.

Rav Beruna transmits teachings in Rav’s name in [Shabbat 21a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.21a.8), 24a and 26a; [Eruvin 63b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.63b.8); [Ketubot 62b:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.62b.3); Sanhedrin 28b; and [Avodah Zarah 38a:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.38a.6) and 40a.[^9] In [Eruvin 85b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.85b.2) Rabbi Elazar (who came from the Land of Israel to Babylonia) said to Rav Beruna, “Did Rav say so?” He said to him, “Yes.” “Show me his lodging”; he showed him. In [Pesachim 106a–b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.106a.13-106b.1), Rav Beruna rules in Rav’s name that one who washes his hands should refrain from reciting kiddush. Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta said to him: “Rav has not yet died, and we have already forgotten his teachings,” etc.

He likewise received from Shmuel, as in [Eruvin 74a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.74a.6): Rav Beruna was sitting and saying this teaching (of Shmuel); Rabbi Elazar, the student, said to him, “Did Shmuel say so?” He said, “Yes.” He said to him, “Show me his lodging”; he showed him. He was very dear to Rabbi Elazar, as in [Berakhot 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.9b.18), where Rabbi Elazar (so is the reading in Dikdukei Soferim and Seder HaDorot) said to Ulla: “When you go there, ask after the welfare of Rav Beruna my brother in the presence of the whole group, for he is a great man and rejoices in mitzvot. Once he joined redemption to prayer, and laughter did not leave his mouth the whole day.”

We likewise find him with Rav Yehudah, as in [Eruvin 60a:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.60a.5): Rav Beruna posed a contradiction to Rav Yehudah at the press of the house of Rav Chanina (Seder HaDorot reads bar Chanina, and Dikdukei Soferim: of the house of Seta).[^8]

In [Avodah Zarah 11b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.11b.10) (11a in Hyman’s citation), Rav Yehudah permitted Rav Beruna to sell wine during the festival of the Tayya’i. Hyman finds only Rav Tavla transmitting a teaching in Rav Beruna’s name. In [Sanhedrin 28b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.28b.25), Rabbi Tanchum cites Rabbi Tavla, who cites Rav Beruna in Rav’s name.[^7] And we find Rabbah bar Beruna; perhaps he …

notes.text: The supplied Pesachim103a is retained, with saved Davidson103b’s continuation proving the STUDENTS ask Yeiva for the cup, not Yeiva addressing them; supplied דבר is read Saba, matching that witness. The lodging and rejoicing episodes and Rif/DikdukeiSoferim variants remain. The final אולי ה breaks off mid-word: p005 held, without completing Hyman from a different work.

The supplied Pesachim locator is 103a, while the saved Davidson continuation at 103b has Rav Yeiva Saba and the students saying “Give us [the cup] and let us bless.” The translation accordingly makes the students address Yeiva, and reads supplied דבר as Saba, following that witness. This is not printed-word verification.

The lodging and rejoicing episodes and their speaker directions remain as supplied. The press in p004 is not independently identified as a winepress. The supplied alternate place forms are attributed to Seder HaDorot and Dikdukei Soferim; the inherited note’s Rif reference is unsupported by this notice and is corrected here. The final אולי ה breaks off mid-word, so neither its continuation nor a relationship to Rabbah bar Beruna is invented.

The supplied Hebrew ends midword. Hyman’s printed entry (vol. I, p. 294) completes the sentence: “We also find Rabbah bar Beruna. Perhaps he was his son.” Shabbat 110a:6 names Rabbah bar Beruna. Hyman proposes the identification of his father.

The meal in Pesachim begins on 103a and continues on 103b. Hyman’s printed entry reads רב ייבא סבא (“Rav Yeiva the Elder”), as does the consulted text. Rav Beruna attributes the ruling about kiddush to Rav at the end of 106a. At the start of 106b, the consulted English takes Rav Yitzchak’s reply to mean that Rav had died only recently. The consulted Sanhedrin 28b adds Rabbi Tanchum at the head of the chain through Rabbi Tavla, Rabbi Beruna and Rav. The wine sale cited by Hyman at Avodah Zarah 11a appears at 11b:10 in the consulted edition, in a discussion of a festival without a fixed date.

The consulted Hebrew of Eruvin 85b names Rabbi Eliezer in the exchange about Rav. The accompanying English gives Rabbi Elazar, and the Hebrew at Eruvin 74a names Rabbi Elazar in the parallel exchange about Shmuel. The consulted Berakhot 9b names Rabbi El’a as the speaker addressing Ulla. The variant names Hyman cites from Dikdukei Soferim and Seder HaDorot are his reports.

The report at [Sanhedrin 28b:25](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.28b.25) includes Rabbi Tanchum as the outer transmitter. The reports at [Eruvin 74a:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.74a.6) and [85b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.85b.2) ask about rulings of Shmuel and Rav respectively. [Seder HaDorot 806](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=806&lang=en) records both exchanges and lists Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi El’ai as variant speakers in the greeting in [Berakhot 9b:18](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.9b.18).
The Eruvin 63b and Ketubot 62b passages each have Beruna transmit in Rav’s name. Eruvin 60a instead has him put a question to Rav Yehudah about Shmuel’s teaching, at the press of Rav Chanina’s house.

Rav Beruna cites Rav on locusts burned in a fire set by a gentile. In the ensuing objection, [Avodah Zarah 38a:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.38a.7) has Rav Chanan bar Ami cite Rabbi Pedat in Rabbi Yochanan’s name.
